title: Fifth special sitting of 2025
summary: This special sitting, held outside the normal parliamentary term at the request of 39 members, opened at 09:00 with 42 members present. The Speaker said an urgent question from a member could not be taken at a special sitting, and referred the Civil Service Commission chair and deputy chair nominees and the Human Rights Commission deputy chair nominee to committees. Members then debated the Independent Institutions Committee's report on the government's bill on seeking the public's views through a public vote: government-side and allied members backed it, saying it would let citizens be consulted and cut election costs, while MDP members said it was aimed at the 2028 presidential election and that their concerns were ignored. The bill passed 64 to 12, and the Speaker also reminded members to wear formal dress, a matter he said would go to the General Committee.

items.title: Independent Institutions Committee report on the government's bill on seeking the public's views through a public vote (third reading and vote)
items.outcome: debated; passed 64 yes, 12 no, 0 abstain (77 members present, 39 needed)

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Fully supported the report, saying the Constitution requires a law on seeking the public's views.
Argued that with such a law, past decisions on Maldivian territory would have needed public consultation.
Said Europe's democracies use public opinion votes and that the opposition lacked the will to compete in elections.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the bill sets out clear rules for public-opinion votes that the Constitution envisages, and rejected claims that it extends the presidential term.
Said holding presidential and parliamentary elections together would shorten members' terms by about six months and save roughly MVR 70 million.
Said the opposition had given no reason for opposing apart from the term issue, and criticised past MDP-era decisions on allowances.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said he saw the bill as a tool tied to the 2028 presidential election, that the information-paper details are left to later regulations, and that MDP would not vote for it.
Raised a point of order asking the chair to intervene over remarks about a government selling parts of the country.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Cited Dhonfanu residents' protests over land reclamation as an example of public views being ignored, and said MDP would not support the bill.
Said he believed the bill was meant to extend the presidential term and called on people to protest.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Presented the committee report, saying the committee consulted the Vice President's office, Elections Commission, Transparency Maldives, political parties and the public, and passed the amended bill by majority.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Raised a point of order that nobody may speak about how a member will vote, since that is the member's own right under the Rules.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the report, saying past governments made big decisions without asking the public.
Said combined elections would cut costs and shorten the presidential and parliamentary terms, not extend them.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the bill for his party MDA, saying decisions should follow public views, and raised slow-moving island development projects in his constituency.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said MDP concerns, including those raised by the committee's one non-government member, were not accommodated by the government's majority, so MDP would not vote for the bill.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill, saying holding elections together would reduce costs and the government acts for the public's benefit.
Said members should keep discipline and formal dress in the chamber.

decisions: The Civil Service Commission chair and deputy chair nominees were referred to the Independent Institutions Committee.
The Human Rights Commission deputy chair nominee was referred to the Human Rights and Gender Committee.
The bill on seeking the public's views through a public vote passed, 64 yes to 12 no with no abstentions.
The Speaker said breaches of the formal-dress convention would be handled by the chair, and that a written dress rule would be sent to the General Committee.
The Speaker said a further sitting would be held the same day if the committees' reports were ready.

votes.what: Passing the bill on seeking the public's views through a public vote, as reported by the Independent Institutions Committee (93 members in total, 77 present, 39 needed)
